title: Cross-Lingual Homogeneity: Do Models Share the SAME Low-Resource Blind Spots?

original_idea.body:
# Cross-Lingual Homogeneity: Do Models Share the SAME Low-Resource Blind Spots?

**Problem:** Whether independent models share the SAME cross-lingual blind spots (so a multilingual jailbreak transfers ecosystem-wide) is a model-homogeneity question that hasn't been framed as such.

**Direction:** Translate safety-relevant prompts into several lower-resource languages. Run ~8 open multilingual models and measure whether the SAME prompts cause correlated safety failures across models.

**Why it matters:** Shared multilingual blind spots mean one translation-based attack defeats the whole ecosystem.

**Relevant context:** LLM safety failures in low-resource languages; shared-blind-spot framing from Artificial Hivemind.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (shared multilingual blind spots -> one attack defeats ecosystem) with systemic framing, but a measurement from mitigation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference plus translation; translation quality is a minor confound manageable with public sets.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: correlated safety failures by language across models; clear endpoint.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models/translations; lab-deprioritized multilingual safety angle.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on multilingual models; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Per-model low-resource failures documented; cross-model shared-blind-spot framing partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Low-resource failures documented per-model; cross-model shared-blind-spot slice is open.
